scope: One short first-school-mock AQA AS Chemistry alkane chain-length trend recall card; conservative reconciliation of 11 older unmapped organic points. No duplicate original ID or mechanistic procedural instructions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: As an unbranched alkane's chain gets longer, what happens to its boiling point?
cards.back: It increases because larger molecules have stronger induced dipole–dipole forces.
accept: Boiling point rises with carbon chain length.
Longer-chain alkanes generally boil at higher temperatures.
It goes up because molecules have more electrons and stronger London forces.
reject: Boiling point falls as alkane chains become longer.
The boiling point stays constant for all alkanes.
Longer alkane chains have weaker intermolecular forces and lower boiling points.
